clue.text: One lessening impact, or adding shine?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device that absorbs a blow, as on a railway carriage
second meaning: one who buffs, polishing something to a shine

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful coinage: someone who buffs a surface is, literally, a buffer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushioning device softens collisions, while the playful agent noun from 'buff' names a polisher.

clue.text: Skirt next to lap

parts.note: by means beside, next to
to lap a runner is to pass them

explanation.surface: A skirt laid next to someone's lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like the garment and 'lap' a part of the body; skirt is a verb meaning go around, and lap means overtake.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt a town is to go round its edge, avoiding it, which is what bypassing it means.

clue.text: Reformist's new blazer

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into something fresh, rearranged

parts.note: the word reformist, with the 's read as 'is', a link joining it to its indicator

explanation.surface: A reforming politician has a new jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and gives no letters. 'blazer' looks like a jacket; it is something that blazes.
explanation.definitionFit: A firestorm is an intense, raging fire, so it is something that blazes, a fanciful sense of blazer.

clue.text: Supporter of the arts decapitating nasty piece of work

indicators.note: decapitating means cutting off the head, the first letter

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person

explanation.surface: An arts patron beheads a horrible person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter of the arts' looks like a patron; it is the stand that holds a painter's canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the frame that holds a painting upright while an artist works, literally supporting art.

clue.text: Muscles and digestive passage, for example, digest!

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
the digestive tract is an example of a tract, a bodily passage

explanation.surface: An anatomy lesson on stomach muscles and the gut, ending with a command to take it all in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digest' looks like a verb urging you to absorb the lesson; here it is the noun, a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a brief summary of a longer text, which is what a digest is too.

clue.text: Outsize garment, wet

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: a large top for a girl
second meaning: British slang for a feeble, weak person

explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' looks like an adjective for the garment; it is a noun for a weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is an oversized blouse; as British slang it means a weak or cowardly man.

clue.text: Avant-garde tailors carrying on referring to hairdressers

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the reworked letters hold the word on
avant-garde means radical and experimental, so the letters of tailors are reworked

explanation.surface: Fashionable tailors carrying on about hairdressers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avant-garde' looks like a description of the tailors' style, but it signals the rearrangement; the result then carries the second word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial is a formal or jocular adjective relating to barbers and their work cutting hair.

clue.text: A through train ultimately for the birds?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: of or for birds

parts.note: via means through, by way of

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of the word train

explanation.surface: A through train for the birds, as in worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the birds' is an idiom for worthless, but here means relating to birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian is the adjective relating to birds, so something avian concerns them.

clue.text: Numbers left in games

indicators.note: in means the word for left goes inside the word for games

parts.note: ties are matches, games in a cup competition
went means left, departed

explanation.surface: Numbers of players remaining in games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like remaining; it is the past tense of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties are numbers from twenty to twenty-nine, so the answer names a set of numbers.

clue.text: Huge insult to take effect before the champers!

indicators.note: before puts the effect word in front of the rest

parts.note: to kick in is to take effect, as a drug does
champers here is a jokey word for teeth, things that champ

explanation.surface: A huge insult delivered before the champagne is poured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champers' is British slang for champagne; here it is a whimsical term for teeth, which champ or chew.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick in the teeth is an idiom for a humiliating setback or a cruel snub.

clue.text: Very cold on the way out

definitions.meaning: second meaning: dying, coming to an end

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests stepping out into the frost; the two halves are separate senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishing is British informal for freezing weather, and literally means dying or passing away.

clue.text: Green food almost entirely rejected: beginning on eggs

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the shortened food word is turned round
the word for food loses only its final letter, so almost all of it stays

parts.note: viand is an old word for an item of food

indicators.note: the beginning of the word eggs is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone pushes away almost all their dinner, starting only on the eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: VIAND (food) loses its last letter to give VIAN, which 'rejected' turns into NAIV; then 'beginning on eggs' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone inexperienced and gullible, which is a synonym for innocent and unworldly.

clue.text: Relative from Zurich for example, oddly?

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

parts.note: Zurich is a Swiss city, so it is an example of something Swiss

explanation.surface: Asking whether a family member comes from Zurich, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Zurich stands for SWISS; its odd letters give S, I, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sis is the familiar short form of sister, a family member.

clue.text: Books by similar illustrators initially damaged — you can't do much about that

definitions.text: you can't do much about that

indicators.note: by means next to, so the books come beside the rest

parts.note: like means similar

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word illustrators

parts.note: torn means damaged
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Books placed beside ones by similar artists, initially damaged: an annoyance you must accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' comes first in the clue but its letters OT go last, placed by the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to mean whether you approve or not, the situation stays the same and must be accepted.

clue.text: Bird of umpteen colours, originally seen in brown

indicators.note: seen in means the initials appear placed inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: originally means take the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A bird of many colours spotted, initially, among brown ones.
explanation.walkthrough: O, U and C, the first letters of 'of umpteen colours', go inside TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical bird with a huge, brightly coloured bill.

clue.text: Large boat: vessel extending across a river

indicators.note: extending across means the vessel stretches around the rest

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel
the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in England

explanation.surface: A big boat stretches across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a boat; it is a container. The Tamar is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled sailing boat, often large enough to carry passengers.

clue.text: Time off I certainly required after case of lice!

indicators.note: after means the I and the word for certainly follow the outside letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'

explanation.surface: After a case of head lice, someone insists they certainly need a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of lice' gives L and E, the outer letters; I and SURE follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time spent away from work, which is what time off means.

clue.text: With nothing to lose, workers' associations unlikely to take off

indicators.note: to lose means the word for unions drops the zero

parts.note: trade unions are associations of workers
O is the round figure zero, nothing
tall means unlikely, as in a tall story

explanation.surface: Unions with nothing to lose are unlikely to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like succeeding; it means remove, as software from a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: To uninstall software is to remove it from a computer, taking it off the system.

clue.text: Dismissal, sweeper having received red card?

parts.note: a brush is something that sweeps
a footballer shown a red card is sent off

explanation.surface: A football sweeper being sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweeper' looks like a defensive football position; it is a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush-off is a curt rejection or snub, a dismissive refusal.

clue.text: About double for another fight

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letters
a match is a double, an exact counterpart

explanation.surface: A boxer's double is on hand for another bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents, a repeat bout.

clue.text: Main South Asian dish, curry principally

definitions.note: the main is an old word for the open sea; here it names a sea

parts.note: a balti is a curry dish of South Asian origin, popular in Britain

indicators.note: principally means first, so take the first letter of curry

explanation.surface: A main course menu: a South Asian dish, mostly curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like a main course; it is the poetic word for the sea, and the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic is a sea, and 'the main' is a literary name for the ocean or high sea.

clue.text: Body part: limb almost eaten by wild animal

indicators.note: eaten by means the shortened limb goes inside the animal

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: almost means the limb word drops its final letter

parts.note: an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A limb nearly devoured by a wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the voice box in the throat, an organ of the body.

clue.text: Lovely unruly fight: very good boxing contest in the end

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly scramble or melee

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the word for very good holds the letter

parts.note: pious means devout, very good in a moral sense

indicators.note: in the end means take the last letter of the word contest

explanation.surface: A messy brawl and a good boxing bout, ending well: lovely stuff, says the fight fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' suggests the sport, but it means enclosing; 'very good' here means devout rather than excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumptious means delicious or delightful, so it is an informal synonym for lovely.

clue.text: Field marshal's back in the papers

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for papers

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

indicators.note: back means the final letter

parts.note: the word marshal, with the possessive marking that its back is meant

explanation.surface: A field marshal returns in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field marshal' is a rank, but 'Field' is the definition and 'marshal's back' gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or sphere of activity, as a field of study is.

clue.text: Wizard conjures up ermine jackets

indicators.note: jackets means the outer words enclose the answer, wrapping it

explanation.surface: A wizard magics up some ermine coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' looks like a magician; it is old British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Wizard and super are both dated British exclamations of approval meaning excellent.

clue.text: Starts off summer parties apparently in spring

indicators.note: starts off means the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Summer parties seem to begin in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; it is a source of mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, or a resort built around one.

clue.text: Character shown by cricket side currently going out

indicators.note: shown by puts the two pieces next to each other

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
an air is a manner or character, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A cricket team's character shows as it walks out to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the on side (or leg side) is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is being broadcast now, so it is currently being transmitted.

clue.text: Piece of cake and vegetables ending in tummy — a picnic!

parts.note: a piece of cake is something easy
peas are vegetables

indicators.note: ending in means take the last letter of the word tummy

explanation.surface: Cake and vegetables end up in the stomach at an outdoor meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' and 'a picnic' both look like food; each means a simple task.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No picnic' means hard work, so a picnic is something effortless, which is what the rhyming phrase means.

clue.text: Fictional villain with short hair male friend cut

indicators.note: short means the word for hair loses its final letter

parts.note: fur is the hair of an animal
man means a male

indicators.note: cut means the word for friend has its tail cut off

parts.note: chum is a friend

explanation.surface: A villain sporting a short haircut, with a male friend also given a trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' and 'cut' both suggest haircuts; each removes a last letter, FUR to FU and CHUM to CHU.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Fu Manchu is the criminal mastermind of Sax Rohmer's novels, a famous fictional evil genius.

clue.text: Very long line I cross, for to get ahead

indicators.note: to get ahead means the word for 'for' goes in front of the rest

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A wordy instruction about crossing a line in order to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is the piece placed first; 'to get ahead' sends it to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolix describes writing or speech that is tediously lengthy and wordy.
